## Motivation

Why convert text to numbers?

- Neural networks operate only on numbers  
- Text is symbolic  
- We must encode it numerically  

Pipeline:

$$
\text{Text} \rightarrow \text{Tokens} \rightarrow \text{IDs} \rightarrow
\text{Embeddings} \rightarrow \text{Tensors}
$$

---

## Predictive Modeling Analogy

Classical ML:

$$
(X_1, X_2, \dots, X_k) \rightarrow y
$$

Text modeling (next token prediction):

$$
(t_{i-2},\, t_{i-1}) \rightarrow t_i
$$

Same idea: supervised learning.

---

## Tokenization

Tokenization splits text into:

- Word tokens  
- Subword tokens (BPE)  
- Characters  

Models do **not** understand words —  
they understand **token IDs**.

---

## Example Sentence

```
I love large language models.
```

Tokens:

```
I
love
large
language
models
.
```

---

## Vocabulary $\rightarrow$ Token IDs

$$
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{Token} & \text{ID} \\
\hline
\text{I} & 1 \\
\text{love} & 2 \\
\text{large} & 3 \\
\text{language} & 4 \\
\text{models} & 5 \\
\text{.} & 6
\end{array}
$$

Encoded sentence:

$$[1,2,3,4,5,6]$$

---

## Context Window

Assume:

- context length = 2  
- predict the next token  

Training examples:

$$
[I,\, love] \rightarrow large
$$

$$
[love,\, large] \rightarrow language
$$

$$
[large,\, language] \rightarrow models
$$

$$
[language,\, models] \rightarrow .
$$

---

## Embedding Layer

Token IDs $\rightarrow$ embedding vectors  
Embedding dimension = **3**

$$
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{Token} & \text{Embedding} \\
\hline
\text{I} & (0.1, 0.2, 0.3) \\
\text{love} & (-0.5, 0.1, 0.0) \\
\text{large} & (0.7, -0.2, 0.4) \\
\text{language} & (0.0, 0.3, 0.9) \\
\text{models} & (0.4, 0.4, 0.4) \\
\text{.} & (-0.2, 0.0, 0.1)
\end{array}
$$

---

## Converting Tokens to Embeddings

Example input:

```
[I, love] = [1, 2]
```

Embedding lookup:

```
1 $\rightarrow$ (0.1, 0.2, 0.3)
2 $\rightarrow$ (-0.5, 0.1, 0.0)
```

Input tensor (2 × 3):

$$
\begin{pmatrix}
0.1 & 0.2 & 0.3 \\
-0.5 & 0.1 & 0.0
\end{pmatrix}
$$

---

## Full Training Examples

Context length = 2, embed dim = 3:

$$
[1,2] \rightarrow
\begin{pmatrix}
0.1 & 0.2 & 0.3 \\
-0.5 & 0.1 & 0.0
\end{pmatrix}
$$

$$
[2,3] \rightarrow
\begin{pmatrix}
-0.5 & 0.1 & 0.0 \\
0.7 & -0.2 & 0.4
\end{pmatrix}
$$

$$
[3,4] \rightarrow
\begin{pmatrix}
0.7 & -0.2 & 0.4 \\
0.0 & 0.3 & 0.9
\end{pmatrix}
$$

$$
[4,5] \rightarrow
\begin{pmatrix}
0.0 & 0.3 & 0.9 \\
0.4 & 0.4 & 0.4
\end{pmatrix}
$$

Targets:

$$[3,4,5,6]$$

---

## Next Token Prediction

The model learns:

$$
f: \mathbb{R}^{2 \times 3} \rightarrow \text{Probability over tokens}
$$

Example output:

- P(large) = 0.72  
- P(language) = 0.10  
- P(models) = 0.08  

Prediction = argmax.

---

## Regression Analogy

| Text Concept | Regression Equivalent |
|--------------|-----------------------|
| Previous tokens | Input \(X\) |
| Next token | Output \(y\) |
| Token IDs | Encoded categorical vars |
| Embeddings | Learned numeric features |
| Context window | \# predictors |
| Sequence model | Regression function |

---

## Comparing Tiny Dataset vs Real LLM Data

Our toy example:

- 6 tokens  
- vocab size = 6  
- context length = 2  
- embed dim = 3  
- 4 training samples  

LLMs: trillions of tokens.

---

## ChatGPT / GPT-4 Data

- 2–10 trillion tokens  
- Books, web, code, math  
- Embedding dim $\approx$ 10,000  
- Context $\approx$ 128k–1M  

---

## Gemini Data

- Trillions of tokens  
- Heavy multimodal  
- Embeddings $\approx$ 8–16k  
- Context $\approx$ 1M  

---

## Grok Data

- Trillions of tokens  
- Real-time X/Twitter  
- Code, web, books  
- Context $\approx$ 128k–1M  

---

## Summary: Tiny vs Massive

| Feature | Example | ChatGPT | Gemini | Grok |
|--------|---------|---------|--------|------|
| Tokens | 6 | trillions | trillions | trillions |
| Vocab | 6 | ~100k | ~100k | ~100k |
| Embedding dim | 3 | ~10k | ~10k | ~8k |
| Context | 2 | 1e5–1e6 | 1e6 | 1e5–1e6 |
| Data size | 1 sentence | internet-scale | internet-scale | internet-scale |

---

## Key Takeaways

- Same pipeline for small and huge models  
- Only scale changes  
- LLMs = same math, more compute
